I am 58 years old and have farmed cotton in Quzhou County for 40 years. My father taught me, and I know this land well. My farm is 10.1 mu—just enough for my wife and me to manage with our well irrigation. I finished primary school, but my real education has been in the fields. I watch what my neighbors do, especially the older farmers in my village whose judgment I trust.

This year, like most years, I will plant cotton on all 10.1 mu. Cotton is our main crop here, and the local market is reliable. I will buy improved cotton seeds from the agricultural supply shop—probably a variety like 99-1 or something similar that has done well locally. I do not save my own seeds anymore; the bought seeds resist pests better and germinate more evenly. Before planting in late April, I will run the rotary tiller over the field. That is what everyone here does, and at my age I cannot manage deep plowing with just two of us.

For fertilizer, I will spread about 100 kg of compound fertilizer across the whole field as a basal dose, and then topdress with about 30 kg of urea during the growing season when the plants start flowering. That has been my practice for years. I have well irrigation, so I will water twice—once at flowering and once during boll formation—because rainfall is never enough here. Cotton pests are relentless, especially bollworms, so I will spray insecticides regularly, plus a couple of herbicide applications and two or three growth regulator sprays to keep the plants manageable. In total, that means about 17 pesticide applications. If the weather cooperates and I stay on top of the pests, I expect to harvest about 550 kg of seed cotton per mu.
